item.title: Productivity in Remote Work: A Holistic View at Remote Work by Investigating Individual-Level Elements, Interpersonal Dynamics and Organizational Factors
item.description: Purpose – This study aims to examine the factors influencing productivity in remote work environments, a work model that gained prominence during the COVID-19 pandemic. It investigates the interplay of individual, interpersonal, and organizational factors by integrating Self-Efficacy Theory, Social Exchange Theory, and the Job Demand-Control-Support (JDCS) Model.Design/methodology/approach – A mixed-methods approach was adopted within the pragmatic paradigm.
